headline: Calls for official data and action on gynaecological violence
title: PPR violences gynécologiques (A-29) - Ensemble
source_brief: This resolution, defended by DéFI's Gisèle Mandaila and Ecolo's Margaux De Ré, asks the Region to recognise and act against gynaecological and obstetric violence, noting Belgium lacks official statistics or a structured reporting system for it. It calls for better data collection, awareness and more respectful, consent-based medical care during pregnancy and childbirth. Parliament adopted it with 62 votes for and 20 abstentions, the abstentions coming from the MR group.
stake: It shapes how patients are informed and treated during pregnancy, childbirth and perinatal care.
raw_outcome: PPR violences gynécologiques (A-29) - Ensemble — 62 pour, 0 contre, 20 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Asks all 19 communes to create safe spaces for women
title: PPR lieux sûrs pour les femmes (A-192) - Ensemble
source_brief: Presented by Ecolo's Farida Tahar and inspired by a motion passed unanimously in Schaerbeek, this resolution seeks to combat sexist and sexual violence against women, including in political and institutional settings. It sets out six lines of action, encouraging all 19 communes to adopt charters, training, clear independent reporting procedures, prevention and gender mainstreaming. Parliament adopted it unanimously, all groups voting in favour.
stake: It aims to make workplaces, institutions and public life safer for women across Brussels.
raw_outcome: PPR lieux sûrs pour les femmes (A-192) - Ensemble — 81 pour, 0 contre, 0 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Reform of jobseeker availability checks rejected almost unanimously
title: PPR disponibilité des demandeurs d'emploi (A-145) - Ensemble
source_brief: Originally tabled by DéFI and Anders, this resolution sought to abolish the three-member evaluation panel used by Actiris when checking jobseekers' availability for work, while leaving the minister flexibility to set control deadlines. In committee the text was reshaped by MR and cd&v amendments imposing a more rigid framework. The final amended version was rejected by Parliament, with 1 vote for, 80 against and 1 abstention.
stake: It affects how unemployed Brussels residents' job-search efforts are checked and which can affect their benefits.
raw_outcome: PPR disponibilité des demandeurs d'emploi (A-145) - Ensemble — 1 pour, 80 contre, 1 abstention(s). Rejeté.

headline: Backs the Iranian people and condemns the regime's crackdown
title: PPR soutien au peuple iranien (A-236) - Ensemble
source_brief: Tabled by the PS's Latifa Aït Baala with Marc-Jean Ghyssels and Jamal Ikazban, and co-signed across several groups, this resolution responds to the violent repression of peaceful protests in Iran since late December 2025. It calls for Parliament to support the Iranian population, defend their fundamental rights and condemn the regime's crackdown. Parliament adopted it with most members in favour, while the PTB and Open VLD abstained.
stake: It states the Region's official position on human rights abroad, using its international standing as a host of EU and NATO institutions.
raw_outcome: PPR soutien au peuple iranien (A-236) - Ensemble — 66 pour, 0 contre, 16 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Parliament backs new Brussels government in confidence vote
title: Motion de confiance du Gouvernement
source_brief: After more than 600 days without a formed regional government following the June 2024 election, the new Brussels government sought Parliament's confidence at the close of its policy declaration of 23 February 2026. The motion of confidence was approved by 51 votes to 27. The seven majority parties (PS, MR, Open VLD, Les Engagés, Groen, CD&V, Vooruit) voted in favour, while the opposition (PTB, DéFI, Team Fouad Ahidar, Vlaams Belang, Ecolo, N-VA) voted against, criticising the declaration as vague and the budget as not yet voted.
stake: Whether to invest the new government and end the longest government-formation deadlock in the Region's history.
raw_outcome: Motion de confiance du Gouvernement — 51 pour, 27 contre, 0 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Resolution urges immediate ceasefire and aid in Darfur and Sudan
title: PPR Darfour et Soudan (A-215) - Ensemble
source_brief: The resolution (A-215) calls for an immediate and permanent ceasefire in Darfur and Sudan and for the strengthening and securing of humanitarian aid and support arrangements. It was adopted with 72 votes in favour and 3 abstentions; the Open VLD (Anders.) group abstained while nearly all other members voted for it. Sponsors described it as a strong cross-party signal on an often-overlooked humanitarian crisis.
stake: Whether the Brussels Parliament should formally call for a ceasefire and expanded humanitarian access in Sudan.
raw_outcome: PPR Darfour et Soudan (A-215) - Ensemble — 72 pour, 0 contre, 3 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Brussels approves polluter-pays deal making producers fund litter cleanup
title: PO Accord de coopération 9/2/26 (A-264) - Ensemble
source_brief: This ordinance gives assent to an interregional cooperation agreement of 9 February 2026 on Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for certain waste streams and litter. Applying the polluter-pays principle, producers of packaging, tobacco products, wipes and similar items would fund the management of the resulting waste and the related public-cleanliness costs, expected to bring the Region around 50 million euros a year, with 54% of the litter share going to municipalities. It was approved by a large majority; PTB and Team Fouad Ahidar abstained, citing concerns that costs could be passed on to households.
stake: Whether to require producers, rather than the public, to pay for cleaning up the litter their products generate.
raw_outcome: PO Accord de coopération 9/2/26 (A-264) - Ensemble — 62 pour, 0 contre, 17 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Adopting the 2026 regional revenue budget
title: PJO Budget voies et moyens 2026 (A-267) - Ensemble
source_brief: This is the Brussels-Capital Region's revenue budget ("voies et moyens") for 2026, setting out the income the Region expects to collect. It is the first full initial budget after a long period in which the Region operated on provisional twelfths, carrying forward deficits without a clear plan. The majority (PS, MR, Open VLD, Les Engagés, Groen, CD&V, Vooruit) approved it 53-32; the opposition (PTB, DéFI, Team Fouad Ahidar, Vlaams Belang, Ecolo, N-VA) voted against.
stake: It determines the revenue side underpinning all regional spending for 2026.
raw_outcome: PJO Budget voies et moyens 2026 (A-267) - Ensemble — 53 pour, 32 contre, 0 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Adopting the 2026 regional expenditure budget
title: PJO Budget dépenses 2026 (A-268) - Ensemble
source_brief: This is the Brussels-Capital Region's expenditure budget ("budget des dépenses") for 2026, authorising the Region's spending and credits for the year. It accompanies the revenue budget as the Region's first full initial budget after running on provisional twelfths. The majority (PS, MR, Open VLD, Les Engagés, Groen, CD&V, Vooruit) approved it 53-32 against the opposition (PTB, DéFI, Team Fouad Ahidar, Vlaams Belang, Ecolo, N-VA).
stake: It sets how much the Region is authorised to spend across all its policy areas in 2026.
raw_outcome: PJO Budget dépenses 2026 (A-268) - Ensemble — 53 pour, 32 contre, 0 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Formal revenue regulation for the 2026 budget
title: PJ Règlement voies et moyens 2026 (A-270) - Ensemble
source_brief: This is the formal regulation enacting the 2026 revenue budget, a procedural companion to the main revenue budget. It carries the same 2026-budget context, the Region having previously operated on provisional twelfths. The majority approved it 53-32 against the opposition, on the same line as the budget itself.
stake: It formally enacts the Region's 2026 revenue budget.
raw_outcome: PJ Règlement voies et moyens 2026 (A-270) - Ensemble — 53 pour, 32 contre, 0 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Formal expenditure regulation for the 2026 budget
title: PJ Règlement dépenses 2026 (A-271) - Ensemble
source_brief: This is the formal regulation enacting the 2026 expenditure budget, a procedural companion to the main expenditure budget. It carries the same 2026-budget context, the Region having previously operated on provisional twelfths. The majority approved it 53-32 against the opposition, on the same line as the budget itself.
stake: It formally enacts the Region's 2026 expenditure budget.
raw_outcome: PJ Règlement dépenses 2026 (A-271) - Ensemble — 53 pour, 32 contre, 0 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Allowing pensions of former Brussels MPs to be indexed
title: P Décision indexation pensions (A-263) - Ensemble
source_brief: This decision amends the rules on pensions paid to former members of the Brussels-Capital Parliament so that they can be indexed (raised in line with cost of living). Those pensions are calculated on federal MP salaries, which the federal level has decided not to index until 2029, automatically freezing the Brussels pensions unless a separate decision provides otherwise. The text was approved with all parties in favour except PTB, which argued these pensions are already far higher than average pensions and voted against.
stake: It restores indexation for former Brussels MPs' pensions that would otherwise stay frozen.
raw_outcome: P Décision indexation pensions (A-263) - Ensemble — 69 pour, 14 contre, 2 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Update tax-cooperation rules to cover crypto-asset addresses
title: PJO adresse de registre distribué (A-274) - Ensemble
source_brief: The ordinance amends the definition of a "distributed-ledger address" in article 5, 31° of the 2013 ordinance that transposed EU Directive 2011/16/EU on administrative cooperation in the field of taxation. The change aligns Brussels rules for sharing tax information on crypto-assets with the relevant EU framework. Parliament adopted it unanimously (78 present, 78 in favour).
stake: It determines how Brussels tax authorities identify and exchange information on crypto-asset holdings held via distributed-ledger (blockchain) addresses.
raw_outcome: PJO adresse de registre distribué (A-274) - Ensemble — 78 pour, 0 contre, 0 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Block conflict-of-interest motion against federal police-merger bill
title: MOTION conflit d’intérêts (A-273) - Art. 91.4
source_brief: Members of DeFI and Ecolo tabled a conflict-of-interest motion (art. 91.4) asking to pause federal bill no. 56-1342, which reforms Belgium's police law and would merge Brussels' six local police zones. The committee recommended rejecting the motion, and Parliament adopted that rejection by 50 votes to 28. PS, MR, Open VLD, Les Engages, Groen, CD&V, Vooruit and N-VA backed rejecting the motion; DeFI, Team Fouad Ahidar, PTB, Ecolo and Vlaams Belang did not.
stake: It decides whether the Brussels Parliament formally objects to and delays the federal plan to merge the region's local police zones.
raw_outcome: MOTION conflit d’intérêts (A-273) - Art. 91.4 — 50 pour, 28 contre, 0 abstention(s). Adopté.

headline: Rejected bid to fast-track an inquiry into Anderlecht social-housing company
title: Urgence A-293 (Com. enq.)
source_brief: Opposition members asked Parliament to urgently take up and immediately debate a proposal to set up a parliamentary commission of inquiry into the management of the Foyer anderlechtois, a public social-housing company, following a news report raising questions about how it is run. The majority refused to treat the request as urgent, sending the text instead to the Finance and General Affairs Committee for its scheduled 1 June meeting. The urgency vote was 25 for, 51 against, with 1 abstention.
stake: Whether an inquiry into a public housing company's management would start at once or wait weeks for the normal committee timetable.
raw_outcome: Urgence A-293 (Com. enq.) — 25 pour, 51 contre, 1 abstention(s). Rejeté.

headline: Rejected bid to fast-track conflict-of-interest motion over tuition-fee hike
title: Urgence A-294
source_brief: Opposition members asked Parliament to urgently take up a conflict-of-interest motion targeting a French Community (Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles) draft decree, including a rise in university tuition fees toward 1,250 euros, arguing it could shift extra costs onto Brussels municipalities and their public welfare centres (CPAS). They sought urgency because the French Community's plenary vote was due the following Wednesday and wanted time to assess the financial impact. The majority refused to grant urgent treatment, with the opposition voting in favour and the majority against.
stake: Whether Brussels would act before a neighbouring assembly's vote it feared would pass new costs onto local budgets.
raw_outcome: Urgence A-294 — 26 pour, 48 contre, 1 abstention(s). Rejeté.
